Formal Dispute of Claim # [REDACTED] and Report of Professional Misconduct – Kifle Jikamo

[REDACTED] To: <support@growtherapy.com>
March 5, 4:20 PM

To the Grow Therapy Compliance and Billing Departments,

I am writing to formally dispute Claim # [REDACTED] regarding a telehealth appointment on February 3, 2026, with a provider listed on your platform as "Dr. Kifle Jikamo." This claim constitutes billing for services not rendered and involves the misrepresentation of professional credentials.

1. Billing for Services Not Rendered The appointment scheduled for February 3rd lasted less than five minutes. Immediately upon joining the session, the provider stated he could not provide treatment for Buprenorphine due to platform policy and an inability to conduct urine screenings via telehealth. Despite providing zero clinical assessment, diagnosis, or treatment, and terminating the session immediately, a claim was submitted to my insurance, L.A. Care Health Plan (Medi-Cal), for a full session. This claim has been processed as "Paid."

2. Comparison of Standard of Care On February 2, 2026, I had an appointment scheduled with another provider on your platform, [REDACTED]. She handled the same medical inquiry ethically by messaging me prior to the session to clarify she could not prescribe the medication. She then canceled the appointment without billing my insurance. This demonstrates that your platform and its providers have the capability to decline care without engaging in fraudulent billing.

3. Misrepresentation of Credentials The provider is listed on Grow Therapy as "Dr. Kifle Jikamo." However, his profile credentials specify "PMHNP-BC, MSN." In the state of California, under Business and Professions Code Section 2054, it is illegal for a healthcare professional to use the title "Dr." in a clinical setting in a manner that misleads patients into believing they are a licensed physician (MD/DO). As an MSN (Master of Science in Nursing) holder, this use of "Dr." is a direct misrepresentation. Even for those with a DNP (Doctorate of Nursing Practice), California law requires explicit clarification of their role as a Nurse Practitioner to avoid patient confusion.

Required Action: I demand an immediate reversal of Claim # [REDACTED] and a formal notification to L.A. Care Health Plan that this claim was submitted in error. I also request a review of this provider's use of the "Dr." title on your platform.

Please be advised that this matter is also being reported to the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) Medi-Cal Fraud Division and the California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN) for further investigation into unprofessional conduct and billing irregularities.

I look forward to your prompt confirmation that this claim has been reversed.

Sincerely,

Nicolas_Hernandez

----
Sent securely from [REDACTED]
